title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Google Gemini 4 Hydrogen (Nov 12-13): agentic tasks reported 2.5x faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, four reasoning levels
bullets.summary: Google's new Gemini 4 model is rolling out in Search and the Gemini API with four selectable reasoning levels; the 2.5x speed figure on agentic tasks is reported, not independently benchmarked.
bullets.how: The Construct: test it as a cheap, fast tier for high-volume batch steps (page checks, feed cleanup) against current defaults before switching anything. PRAGMA: selectable reasoning levels are a cost lever to show clients. Brand 9 Signs: indirect, via whatever it powers in Google Search answers.

bullets.title: HeyGen Decision 1 model (Nov 13) added to HeyGen's developer platform
bullets.summary: HeyGen published a new model, Decision 1, in its developer docs; no benchmark numbers have been released yet.
bullets.how: Brand 9 Signs: a candidate for short product and install videos once we can see what it does; check whether it is reachable from the Higgsfield/HeyGen tooling we already use. The Construct: add to the video-generation watchlist. PRAGMA: no.

bullets.title: ElevenLabs ElevenAI preview (Nov 14): meeting transcription + dictation in 90+ languages + agent follow-up actions
bullets.summary: ElevenLabs combined transcription, multilingual dictation and its ElevenAgent so a meeting can end with drafted follow-up actions; access is by early-access signup.
bullets.how: The Construct: overlaps with Claude Meetings (beta); compare the two before adding either to client-call workflows. Brand 9 Signs: voice notes from site visits could become quotes and tasks. PRAGMA: a voice-to-action pattern for operator clients.

bullets.title: United Airlines will restrict unauthorized third-party AI agents from its booking systems (Nov 13)
bullets.summary: A major consumer brand is moving to block outside agents from transacting on its site, the opposite direction from the open agent-checkout push (ChatGPT Wallet).
bullets.how: The Construct: our browser-driven loops (partner orders at Signs365, supplier sites) can be blocked the same way; prefer official APIs/MCP where they exist and keep a manual fallback. Brand 9 Signs: decide deliberately whether brand9signs.com welcomes shopping agents (we do, via feeds). PRAGMA: 'agent access policy' is a client advisory item.

bullets.title: MCP ecosystem census (Nov 14): about 118,000 active MCP servers and 52,000 agent skills
bullets.summary: HostedMCP's November report counts 118,434 active MCP servers and 52,147 agent skills as of Nov 14; new enterprise servers keep landing (e.g. digna's on-prem data MCP server, Nov 15).
bullets.how: The Construct: at this volume, discovery is no longer the problem, vetting is; keep the installed-skills registry curated and security-reviewed. PRAGMA: curation and vetting of MCP servers is sellable. Brand 9 Signs: no signage-specific MCP server surfaced today.

praxis_lesson: When outside sites start blocking agents, the browser path is the fragile one: for every loop that drives someone else's website, know the official API or MCP route and keep a manual fallback ready. With 118k MCP servers out there, the edge is choosing and vetting, not finding.
